headline: Google loses $4.7B EU antitrust fine over Android practices
summary: Europe's top court upholds $4.7B fine on Google
details: The European Court of Justice upheld a $4.7B fine on Google over alleged anti-competitive practices related to Android. The fine was initially imposed by the European Commission in 2018.
The Commission found that Google abused Android's dominance to give unfair advantage to its own apps via pre-installation deals with smartphone makers.
This is not Google's only run-in with EU antitrust regulators, who have also fined the company for anti-competitive practices in its advertising technology business.

headline_marked: AI Agent 'Darwin' Evolves Its Own Prompts [[Self-Improvement Loop]] Safeguards
headline: AI Agent 'Darwin' Evolves Its Own Prompts Self-Improvement Loop Safeguards
summary: Developer creates AI framework that lets agents rewrite their own prompts while preventing degradation.
details: A developer built a TypeScript framework called 'Darwin' that allows AI agents to rewrite their own prompts and improve over time. The framework includes safeguards to prevent the agent from drifting into worse performance.
The AI agent uses a critic to evaluate its output and propose new prompts. However, this process can lead to issues like optimizing for the wrong signal or eroding constraints.
To address these issues, the developer implemented four key safeguards: regression rollback, data-quality guards, alignment checks, and statistically honest A/B testing.
These safeguards ensure that the agent's performance does not degrade over time and that any changes to the prompt are thoroughly evaluated.
The developer spent three months building the framework and highlighted the importance of the safeguards in preventing the agent from getting worse.
caption:
Can AI agents safely rewrite their own prompts? A new framework says yes.

A developer built a TypeScript framework called 'Darwin' that allows AI agents to rewrite their own prompts and improve over time. The framework includes safeguards to prevent the agent from drifting into worse performance.

The AI agent uses a critic to evaluate its output and propose new prompts. However, this process can lead to issues like optimizing for the wrong signal or eroding constraints.

To address these issues, the developer implemented four key safeguards: regression rollback, data-quality guards, alignment checks, and statistically honest A/B testing.

These safeguards ensure that the agent's performance does not degrade over time and that any changes to the prompt are thoroughly evaluated.

The developer spent three months building the framework and highlighted the importance of the safeguards in preventing the agent from getting worse.
